Recent code discovered in the WhatsApp TestFlight beta suggests Meta is exploring alternatives to iCloud backups for iPhone users. Details below.

WhatsApp is developing its own backup service

According to findings by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is developing its own cloud backup service for iPhone users, offering an alternative to iCloud.

The feature is not yet available to TestFlight beta users, but WABetaInfo has successfully enabled the relevant interface, allowing users to choose between iCloud or WhatsApp's own cloud service as their backup destination. The interface shows that 2GB of free storage will be provided, and the report also mentions that paid plans can offer up to 1TB of capacity.

The report also points out that users can currently choose whether WhatsApp backups on iCloud use end-to-end encryption, while WhatsApp's own backup system will use end-to-end encryption by default.

Although no specific launch timeline has been announced, the report notes that WhatsApp is also developing a Google Drive backup alternative for Android users. Given that development work for both platforms is progressing simultaneously, the new feature could be officially announced in the near future.
